objects.name: SSP Brick (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Construct a SSP (Stabilized Single Point) Brick element from an eight vertex mesh.
The mesh is reordered into the node order OpenSees wants and checked for a positive Jacobian at every corner - a brick wound the wrong way round, or twisted, is one the solver accepts and answers with the wrong sign rather than rejecting.

A solid has no local axes. OpenSees gives neither element an orientation argument, and an nD material has no orientation either, so the material's own directions - Ex, Ey and Ez on an Elastic Orthotropic - are the global X, Y and Z, and so are the stresses read back. To align an orthotropic material with the part, rotate the model.
Where a solid meets a beam or a shell at a point, the two are tied in translation only: a solid node carries no moment, so the junction is a pin.

objects.name: Topology Optimisation (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Finds where a solid needs its material. Every solid of the model - SSP Bricks, Ten Node or Four Node Tetrahedra - gets a density between 0 and 1 and a stiffness of density cubed, and the densities are found that make the model stiffest under its loads with VolumeFraction of the material: SIMP with the optimality criteria update and a density filter, as top3d. Removed material is never cut out: a void element keeps a billionth of its stiffness, so the mesh stays as it is.
Bricks are solved as OpenSees' eight point brick (stdBrick), on the same nodes, because an SSP Brick fixes part of its stiffness when it is built. Every solid needs an Elastic Isotropic Material. Beams, shells and links in the model take no part: they keep their full stiffness. One OpenSees stays open for the whole run.
Set Run to true to start. The outputs follow the run as it goes. Switching Run off pauses it; on again, it goes on from where it stopped, and so does a run given more Iterations or a smaller Tolerance after it ended. Changing any other input starts it again from the beginning.
Once it stops, AlpacaModel is the design as a model of its own, solid and void, to analyse.

objects.name: Analysis Settings (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Collects everything OpenSees needs in order to solve - constraint handler, numberer, system of equations, convergence test, solution algorithm, integrator and stepping - into the one object Run Analysis takes.
Every input has a default, so an unconnected component already describes a valid linear static analysis. For a dynamic one set AnalysisType to Transient, and give it a Newmark or Central Difference Integrator, an Analysis Step with Dt, and a Damping.

objects.name: Run Analysis (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Writes the assembled model out as an OpenSees script, solves it, and returns the model with its results attached.
Results are recorded to a recorder.mpco file beside the Grasshopper document and read back by the 08_NumericalOutput components; an MPCO Recorder connected to Assemble Model chooses what the file holds, and what it is called. When a run fails the AlpacaModel output comes out empty - read the log output to find out why.

objects.name: View Results_WIP (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Draw any result on the model: displacements, beam force diagrams, beam stresses, shell forces, shell stresses, solid stresses, reactions.
Pick the result, the component and the unit from the dropdowns. ElementId shows only some of the elements and greys the rest, so what you are looking at stays in the model around it.
With Extruded beams on, beam stresses that differ across a section - σx, σMy, σMz, τV, τT, Von Mises - are painted point by point over it; drawn as lines, each section shows its worst.
Work in progress, and meant to grow into the replacement for the separate view components.

objects.desc: A panel for custom notes and text values
objects.text:
Bridge - a Topology Optimisation example.

The design domain is a steel block 16 m long, 2 m wide and 4 m high, pinned along both ends of its bottom. Its top layer is the deck: it carries 10 kN/m2 and is kept solid, by its ElementId, through Keep. The optimisation finds the fifth of the rest that carries the deck stiffest: an arch from support to support rising into the deck at mid-span, with a column up to the deck near each end.

1. Set Run to true. The run goes on its own thread: the Surface preview and the outputs follow it, about once a second, and Rhino stays free.
2. Set Run to false to pause, true to go on; raise Iterations to go further. Change anything else - VolumeFraction, Bricks per metre - and the run starts again.
3. Drag Step back to watch the run again, design by design: every iteration is kept.
4. Bricks per metre 3 gives 3 456 bricks, about 15 s on an M2 Pro; 4 gives 8 192, under a minute. At 2 the deck is a 0.5 m slab of solid steel, stiff enough to span most of the way, and the steel goes into two legs that shorten its span instead of an arch.
5. Once the run has stopped, enable Run Analysis and Legend (select both, right-click, Enable): AlpacaModel is the design as a model of its own - the solid bricks at full stiffness, the void ones gone, with the supports and loads that stand on them - and View Results colours it by Von Mises stress. Disable Run Analysis again before dragging Step, or every design shown is analysed.

Each SSP Brick is solved as OpenSees' eight point brick: the SSP Brick fixes part of its stiffness when it is built, so it cannot be softened. A void brick keeps a billionth of its stiffness; nothing is cut out of the mesh. Topology Optimisation needs a license.
